h1: How to Sell Online Courses Without a Monthly Subscription
dek: Monthly bills, pay-per-sale commission or one predictable annual plan: what each really costs an Indian educator at every sales level, when a monthly 0% plan with no lock-in makes sense, and how to pick the one that fits your stage.
cover_alt: Sell online courses without a monthly subscription: monthly bill vs pay per sale vs one annual plan compared
audience: Indian educators, tutors and coaching institute owners choosing how to pay for a course-selling platform
author_note: AllCoaching sells both yearly plans and monthly 0% plans, so this guide shows the maths at every sales level, names where a pay-per-sale or another platform's plan costs less, and links every competitor figure to its official page.
intro: You can sell online courses without a monthly subscription in two ways: a pay-per-sale platform that takes a percentage of every sale and charges no fixed fee, or one annual plan with a smaller fee on sales (or none). Pay-per-sale usually costs least while sales are small; an annual plan costs less once yearly sales grow, from about ₹5 lakh in the examples below. If you are happy to pay monthly, a plan with 0% commission and no lock-in can leave you more once sales are steady.

Most educators meet the monthly bill at the worst moment. You teach SSC maths in Hindi on YouTube, or spoken English on Instagram, and decide to sell your first course. The platform you like bills you every month, in the months you sell well and in the months you sell nothing, such as the weeks after an exam when students disappear.

This guide compares the three ways to pay for a course platform: a monthly subscription, pay per sale and an annual plan. It works out what each costs from no sales to ₹20 lakh a year, using published prices, and shows where each one wins. All cost figures are illustrative and before GST unless we say otherwise.
takeaways: There are two ways to avoid a monthly bill: pay per sale (a percentage of each sale, no fixed fee) or one annual plan with a smaller fee on sales, or 0%.
Pay per sale costs least at small sales. With 10% on every sale, ₹1 lakh of sales costs ₹10,000 a year, before add-ons such as your own app or website.
An annual plan costs less as sales grow. In our worked table, an annual plan with a lower fee starts to cost less than a 10% commission at about ₹5 lakh of yearly sales.

AllCoaching offers both (before GST): yearly plans from ₹6,999 + 10% with no monthly bill, or monthly plans at 0% commission from ₹3,999 with no lock-in. Below about ₹4 lakh of yearly sales, a yearly plan usually costs least; above that, a monthly 0% plan usually leaves you more.
Compare yearly totals, not headline prices. Add GST, gateway charges and every add-on you need, such as a branded app, website or custom domain.
A monthly bill is not the problem on its own; a lock-in and a fee on top are. If you pay monthly, look for 0% commission and no lock-in, and compare what each 0% plan includes, not only its price.

sections.h2: Can you sell online courses without a monthly subscription?
sections.html:
Yes. A course platform charges you in one of three ways: a fixed monthly subscription, a percentage of every sale with no fixed fee (pay per sale), or one annual plan, usually with a smaller percentage on sales. Only the first one sends you a bill every month.

{{fig:three-models|Three ways to pay for a course platform when you sell online courses: monthly subscription, pay per sale commission, or annual plan with a smaller fee|Three pricing models. Each one is the lowest-cost choice at a different stage.}}
ModelWhat you payIn a month with no salesCosts least when
Monthly subscriptionA fixed bill every month, sometimes plus a fee on salesThe full monthly billSales are high and steady all year
Pay per sale (commission only)A percentage of every sale, no fixed feeNothing for the planSales are small or uncertain
Annual plan + smaller feeOne yearly bill and a lower percentage, or 0%No new bill; the plan is already paidSales are growing or already large

The search "course platform without monthly fee" usually comes from one worry: paying a bill before you earn. Pay per sale removes that worry completely. An annual plan removes the monthly bill, but you pay once for the year, so it suits an educator who expects to sell steadily.

If you are still deciding what an academy of your own includes, start with what an online academy is, then come back to the costs.

sections.h2: Why a monthly subscription is hard on a new academy
sections.html:
A monthly subscription is hard on a new academy because the bill is fixed while teaching income is not. Your sales move with exam calendars, admission seasons and your own launch dates, but the bill arrives on the same date every month.

{{fig:monthly-vs-annual|Monthly subscription with 12 bills a year compared with one annual plan when you sell online courses|Twelve renewals a year compared with one. Months marked red are illustrative quiet months.}}

Teaching income in India is seasonal. A NEET or JEE educator sells most batches before the exam year starts; a board-exam educator is busy from October to February; a CUET or state PSC educator follows the notification. Between those peaks, many academies sell very little.

A monthly plan also adds twelve renewal moments a year. That pressure pushes many educators to rush a launch or cut a price to cover the next bill, which is the opposite of what a new academy needs.

When a monthly subscription is the right choice

A monthly plan is not wrong in itself. It is the right choice when you want to test a platform for a month or two before committing, or when your sales are high and steady enough that a 0% fee saves more than the monthly bill costs. Check two things before you pick one: that there is no lock-in, so you can stop in a quiet month, and that the plan takes no fee on top of the bill.

Card auto-debits for recurring bills in India run on e-mandates. In June 2022 the Reserve Bank of India raised the limit for recurring card payments that can run without a fresh one-time password from ₹5,000 to ₹15,000 per transaction.[1] If a monthly bill is above that limit, expect to approve the payment yourself, and check the RBI's current e-mandate rules before you rely on auto-debit.

{{q:Is an annual plan just a subscription paid once a year?|Yes, and that is the honest way to describe it. An annual plan is a yearly subscription: you pay once, for twelve months, and renew once a year. The difference from a monthly plan is one bill and one renewal decision instead of twelve, and a known cost for the year on day one.}}

sections.h2: Pay-per-sale course platforms in India: when commission-only costs less
sections.html:
A pay-per-sale course platform charges no fixed fee and keeps a percentage of every sale instead. It costs least when your sales are small, because a month with no sales costs nothing and the fee only grows when your income does.

Two Indian examples, from their official pricing pages checked on 24 October 2026:

  • Exly Starter shows its annual upfront fee as "FREE" with a 10% commission on sales. Its add-ons are priced separately: a mobile app (iOS and Android) from ₹60,000 a year, a custom website from ₹60,000 a year and white-labelled branding from ₹20,000 a year. Source: Exly pricing.
  • TagMango Basic has no fixed fee and a 10% commission that includes the Indian payment gateway, and it is capped at 200 students. A custom domain needs its Freedom Setup at ₹24,999 a year on top of a plan, and all TagMango prices are plus GST. Source: TagMango pricing.

So pay per sale is a good way to test an idea. If you are selling your first ₹50,000 of courses, a 10% commission costs ₹5,000, less than any annual plan.

Where pay per sale stops being the low-cost choice

Two things change as you grow. First, the commission grows with every sale: at ₹10 lakh of yearly sales, 10% is ₹1 lakh a year. Second, the things that make an academy feel like your own, such as your own app, your own website or your own domain, are often priced as add-ons on pay-per-sale plans. Add them and the "no fixed fee" plan has a fixed fee after all.

Pay per sale fits

Testing one course. Uncertain demand. Sales under about ₹2–3 lakh a year. You do not need your own app or domain yet.

Look again when

Sales pass about ₹5 lakh a year. You need your own app, website or domain as paid add-ons. A student cap limits your batch size.

sections.h2: Costs that stay with any course platform
sections.html:
Removing the monthly bill does not remove every cost. Payment gateway charges, GST, add-ons, marketing and your own time stay with you on any platform, so add them before you compare.

{{fig:costs-that-stay|Costs that remain when you sell online courses on any platform: payment gateway charges, GST, add-ons, marketing and student support|Five costs to add to any platform comparison. Logos belong to their owners.}}

Payment gateway charges

Every UPI or card payment passes through a payment gateway. Razorpay's pricing page lists a 2% flat standard fee per transaction and notes 0% MDR on UPI for most transactions, so what you pay depends on how your students pay.[2] Some course platforms include gateway charges in their fee and some add them on top, so ask yours. Our guide to accepting UPI payments for online courses explains checkout in more detail.

GST

Most plan prices in this guide exclude GST, and Indian coaching services are generally taxed at 18% once you are registered. Add GST to every plan price before you compare, and read our guide on GST for coaching institutes for when registration applies.

Add-ons

List every feature you need and check whether it is included or extra: your own Android or iOS app, a website on your own domain, Zoom, branding and extra teacher logins. On some platforms these add-ons cost more each year than the plan itself.

Marketing and your time

No pricing model brings students on its own. You will still teach on YouTube, post on Instagram, answer on WhatsApp and perhaps run ads. Our guides to digital marketing for coaching institutes and Meta ads for coaching institutes cover both free and paid ways to find students.

The market is large enough for every model to exist. IBEF puts India's edtech market at ₹64,875 crore (US$7.5 billion), projected to reach ₹2,50,850 crore by 2030–31.[3]

sections.h2: How to sell online courses without a monthly subscription: 7 steps
sections.html:
Here is the method in order: an afternoon of maths and a two-week trial.

{{steps}} {{cta}}

Choose by your expected yearly sales: pay per sale or a low-priced annual plan while you test an idea, an annual plan with a lower fee as you grow, and a 0% commission plan, monthly or yearly, once sales are large.

{{fig:decision-guide|Decision guide to sell online courses without a monthly subscription by yearly sales stage, from testing an idea to a large academy|A simple guide by stage. Illustrative, before GST and add-ons.}}

Testing an idea · under ₹1 lakh a year

A yoga teacher selling a first ₹1,499 recorded course to 30 students (₹44,970 of sales, illustrative) pays least with pay per sale. If you want your own website, domain and Android app from day one, Starter adds them for ₹6,999 a year plus GST.

Growing · ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh a year

An SSC educator selling a ₹2,999 batch to 120 students (₹3.6 lakh, illustrative) sits in Growth's range. The yearly plan cost is known on day one, and the fee is 7.5% instead of 10%.

Established · ₹5 lakh to ₹15 lakh a year

A NEET biology academy selling ₹8 lakh a year (illustrative) pays ₹64,999 on yearly Pro before GST, against ₹80,000 at a 10% commission and ₹71,988 on monthly Growth at 0%. Above about ₹9.4 lakh, monthly Growth costs less than yearly Pro.

Large · above ₹15 lakh a year

Above ₹15 lakh, a 0% commission plan usually costs least. On AllCoaching that is monthly Growth up to ₹1.5 lakh of sales a month, or monthly Pro (₹7,999 a month, no sales limit, own Android and iOS app), with no lock-in. Compare it with other 0% plans on what they include, such as your own branded apps and domain, not only on price.

If you are still at the first step, read how to create your first online course before you choose a plan; the course decides your price, and the price decides your plan.

sections.h2: Mistakes educators make when avoiding the monthly fee
sections.html:
The most common mistake is comparing the monthly price alone, without adding the fee on sales, GST and add-ons for a full year.

{{fig:mistakes|Mistakes educators make when choosing a course platform without a monthly subscription, and what to do instead|Five mistakes and the fix for each.}}

Each fix takes minutes: work out a full-year total at your sales level, list the add-ons you need, add GST, and confirm that your students and content can be exported if you ever move.

When we talk to educators who switch platforms, the reason is rarely the first-year price. It is usually a cost they did not see coming, such as an app add-on or a fee that grew with their sales, which is why we publish every plan price before anyone signs up.

faq: Can I sell online courses without paying a monthly subscription?

Yes. Use a pay-per-sale platform that takes a percentage of each sale with no fixed fee, or one annual plan with a smaller fee on sales or none. Pay per sale usually costs least at small sales; an annual plan costs less as sales grow. If you do pay monthly, a plan with 0% commission and no lock-in can leave you more once sales are steady.
Which is better for a new educator, pay per sale or an annual plan?

If you expect under about ₹1 lakh of sales in your first year, pay per sale usually costs least on platform cost alone. If you need your own website, domain and app from the start, check what those add-ons cost; a low-priced annual plan that includes them can cost less overall.
At what sales level does an annual plan cost less than a 10% commission?
In our illustrative table, an annual plan with a 5% fee and a ₹24,999 price matches a 10% commission at ₹5 lakh of yearly sales and costs less above it, before GST and add-ons.
Is an annual plan a subscription?
Yes. An annual plan is a yearly subscription that you pay once and renew once a year. It replaces twelve monthly bills with one and fixes your platform cost for the year.
Does AllCoaching have a monthly plan?

Yes. AllCoaching has three monthly plans at 0% commission with no lock-in: Starter ₹3,999 (sales up to ₹50,000 a month), Growth ₹5,999 (up to ₹1.5 lakh a month) and Pro ₹7,999 (no sales limit). If you prefer no monthly bill, the yearly plans are Starter ₹6,999, Growth ₹12,999 and Pro ₹24,999 with a 10%, 7.5% or 5% platform fee. Prices exclude GST, and every plan starts with a 7-day free trial with no card needed.
Which AllCoaching plan costs least for my sales?

Before GST, yearly Starter costs least below about ₹2.4 lakh of yearly sales, yearly Growth to about ₹4.7 lakh, monthly Starter (0%) to ₹6 lakh, yearly Pro to about ₹9.4 lakh, monthly Growth (0%) to ₹18 lakh, and monthly Pro (0%) above that. Put simply: below about ₹4 lakh, a yearly plan usually costs least; above that, a monthly 0% plan usually leaves you more.
Is there a zero commission course platform in India?

Yes, several plans charge 0% on sales for a fixed price. AllCoaching's monthly plans take 0% commission from ₹3,999 a month plus GST, with Pro at ₹7,999 a month (₹95,988 a year) and no sales limit. Learnyst lists 0% transaction fees on Professional at ₹8,099 a month billed annually, which is ₹97,188 a year plus taxes. Compare what each includes.
Are payment gateway charges included in the platform fee?

It depends on the platform. TagMango, for example, says its commission includes the Indian payment gateway. Others add gateway charges on top. Ask the platform before you compare, and check the gateway's own pricing page.
What costs remain if I avoid a monthly subscription?
GST, payment gateway charges, add-ons such as your own app or domain, marketing and your own time. Add these to the plan price and the fee on sales to see your real yearly cost.
glossary: A pricing model where a platform charges a fixed bill every month, whether or not you sell, sometimes with a fee on sales as well.
A pricing model with no fixed fee where the platform keeps a percentage of every sale you make. Also called commission-only pricing.
A yearly subscription paid once for twelve months, usually lower than the same plan billed monthly, and often with a smaller fee on sales.
The percentage of each sale a course platform keeps for its service, such as 10%, 7.5% or 5% on AllCoaching's yearly plans and 0% on its monthly plans.
The sales level at which two plans cost the same in a year. Above it, the plan with the lower percentage costs less.
The service that processes UPI, card and netbanking payments and sends the money to the seller, for a per-transaction charge.
A standing instruction that lets a merchant charge your card or UPI account automatically for recurring payments, under RBI rules.
A feature sold separately from a plan, such as a branded app, custom website, custom domain or extra integrations.
